step1.question: Choose the workspace mode you want to create or attach.

existing.title: Logical Workspace
existing.description: Default mode. Use an existing path or create a new workspace folder without requiring git worktrees.

new.title: Worktree Workspace
new.description: Create or associate a git worktree with explicit branch and base settings.

step2.logicalHelp: Use an existing folder or create a new logical workspace here.
step2.worktreeHelp: Choose the filesystem path where the worktree will live.
step2.existingHelp: Full path to your existing workspace directory
step2.newHelp: Full path to your workspace directory
step2.sourcePathHelp: Required when creating a new worktree. Point this to the repository that owns the base branch.
step2.baseBranchHelp: Optional. If you leave this as-is, the request will use main as the base branch.
step2.worktreeConsequences: Worktree mode creates or links a separate filesystem directory and branch. Deleting it later may also require removing the worktree from the source repository.
step2.githubHelp: Optional: provide a GitHub URL to clone a repository
step2.githubAuthHelp: Only required for private repositories. Public repos can be cloned without authentication.
step2.tokenHelp: This token will be used only for this operation
step2.publicRepoInfo: Public repositories don't require authentication. You can skip providing a token if cloning a public repo.
step2.noTokensHelp: No stored tokens available. You can add tokens in Settings → API Keys for easier reuse.

step3.existingInfo: The workspace will be added to your project list and will be available for Claude/Cursor sessions.
step3.newWithClone: The repository will be cloned from this folder.
step3.newEmpty: The workspace will be added to your project list and will be available for Claude/Cursor sessions.
step3.worktreeInfo: This action will create or attach a separate worktree directory and keep the branch/base relationship visible before any destructive follow-up.
